requirement.native_selected_endpoint: The installed IndexRead route: luma-platform index-review LOGIN READ-GRANT /run/luma-granted-client/requests/<32 hex>/index.json (rust/luma-platform/src/content_index/client.rs:14, content_index/client/admission.rs:18 and 134, content_index/runtime.rs:246). Custody routes Operation::IndexRead (content_custody/protocol.rs:1199) to indexed::with_index (content_custody/indexed.rs), which runs compute::run. Its Query arm (content_custody/indexed/compute.rs:239-240) answers only over the generation the owner's C leaf names as current, never over a caller-chosen manifest, and refuses "no current independently C-selected index generation" or "query chooses a stale/foreign generation". It reads through the native Reader with the native Gate. The leaf field is current_generation (content_custody/v2_publication/index.rs:19). Its only writer is the test-only effects module (index/effects.rs:77; #[cfg(test)] at index.rs:5-7) used by the test-only direct Publish, so a production build has no route that selects a generation and its Query arm refuses every query
requirement.acl_filtered_corpus: The corpus is owner-local: one owner's corpus map in C. The native Gate admits only that owner's read-only Inspect and an admission within the original read's resources (content_custody/indexed/boundary.rs:106-127). Every Gate method re-runs Current::check (content_custody/indexed.rs:91-104), which reads the C-selected index state (three TPM NV anchor reads) and compares it with the request's. Each returned hit is re-proven through current_candidate (boundary.rs:175-186) against the current corpus map, its artifact and its lifecycle, so a revoked, deleted or foreign object refuses. Any refusal withholds the whole output, counts included. total_matches is bound to the exact current corpus root, not proven per unreturned match
requirement.text_and_semantic: CorpusQueryKind::LexicalAnd (lexical AND over postings) and CorpusQueryKind::FeatureLsa (feature-space LSA over the generation's vectors); no model synthesis is involved

implementation: generation/tests/observed.rs (new, test-only): ObservedIndexStore over an Envelope reader shaped like the native Reader (owner and 16 KiB page bound, a debit of maximum+1 from one aggregate 128 MiB reservation before any private read, then a post-read check) and a Counted boundary shaped like the native Gate (the owner's read-only Inspect only, admission within 192 MiB memory, one task and the original read reservation, no writes). request() follows the native Query arm: the selected manifest blob, VerifiedGeneration::open, then query. It counts boundary calls by kind, pages, bytes and debits, and a lower bound on native Current::check calls

observed_native_envelope_generation_queries_match_local_store_and_withhold_on_refusal (new test): four lexical and semantic queries equal the local-store results; each returned hit is re-proven four times and nothing else is; a refused returned hit withholds the whole output; a refused unreturned match does not; a stale or foreign generation, a descriptor that is not the selected manifest, another owner's Inspect or admission, an over-reservation or two-task admission, a borrowed owner, an unbounded or zero page, an exhausted reservation, revocation and a withdrawn C selection each refuse

generation/tests/latency.rs (new, test-only, #[ignore]): nf08_first_result_latency_over_observed_native_query_path. A SplitMix64 corpus over 30,000 Zipf-ranked synthetic words builds through every actual index phase into one published generation, selected as a manifest blob. Seven query classes of 30 samples each (after 3 warm-up queries) run through observed::request with a fresh reservation per request, and every result is checked against the generator's ground truth. It reports the nearest-rank p50, p95 and max of request time, of the time inside the synthetic boundary callbacks and of the rest (the content-store query path), plus pages, debits, boundary calls and the native check lower bound, and the unit cost of one manifest hash

job/tests.rs, projection/tests.rs, vectors/tests.rs and generation/tests.rs (test-only): SCALE_DOCUMENTS (1024), from which the fixtures lift their window caps and job limits and print one nf08-scale line per phase. No default test reaches it

analysis.fan_out: Every request page and every proof goes through the boundary. In cal1024-a a request made about 286 boundary calls per 16 KiB page (61985.2 calls over 216.5 pages on average), and each Counted call stands for at least two native Current::check runs (Gate::current checks before and after its closure), so the native lower bound was 95,461 to 341,623 checks per query
analysis.manifest_hash: Each refresh of Current in query.rs re-serialised the 2,209-byte manifest to canonical JSON and hashed it, at 3.651 microseconds a hash in cal1024-b, and the fixture Guard's current_index_generation (generation/tests.rs:39-52) does the same once more per call. The query.rs half is DATA computed once in Current::new in the measured snapshot; the Guard half is the synthetic boundary's own cost and stays in the boundary time. The native Gate's current_generation (content_custody/indexed/boundary.rs:293-298) also re-serialises and hashes the manifest on every call
analysis.scaling: Not measured beyond 1,024 objects. In cal1024-a both semantic classes read the same 126 pages for every query (mean equals max), so FeatureLsa scans every generation vector; lexical classes read pages in proportion to the postings of their words. Both grow at least linearly with the corpus, so the same path over 100,000 objects would read about 100 times as many pages for a semantic query. Meeting 500 ms at 100,000 objects needs a sub-linear candidate path (for example a bounded top-k over postings or a coarse vector partition) as well as fewer boundary checks per page
analysis.native_cost: The native Current::check reads three TPM NV anchors and compares the C-selected index state on every call. At the measured lower bound of tens to hundreds of thousands of checks per query, native latency cannot meet 500 ms unless a request checks the current state once per page or once per request rather than once per record and proof. That is a change to the native freshness rule and is the owner's security decision; this record proposes nothing that weakens it

native_integration_hooks: A production route that selects a generation: the leaf's current_generation (content_custody/v2_publication/index.rs:19) has no writer outside the #[cfg(test)] effects module (index/effects.rs:77), so a production Query refuses every request

After the direct Publish in actual_index_phases_run_through_c_and_publish_one_generation, run Query through compute::run with the real Gate and Reader, compare its results with the local store's and with observed::request, and assert the stale or foreign generation and borrowed-owner refusals
Count Current::check calls and TPM anchor reads per native query with a counting Checkpoint, so the native lower bound in this record becomes a measured number
In the native Gate's current_generation, hash the immutably borrowed, already validated manifest once per request as DATA, as query.rs now does, without removing any current-state check
An owner decision on per-request or per-page batching of Current::check, and on the time, storage and build path for a 100,000-object generation
not_claimed: The NF08 target. The 448.860 ms p95 is development evidence over 1,024 objects, not 100,000, on a laptop in a container, with a warm page cache and synthetic boundary callbacks; one run per snapshot, so its run-to-run variation is unmeasured

A 100,000-object measurement. At the measured build rate (projection alone took 4175.549 s at 1,024 objects with 512 features) a 100,000-object generation is outside one bounded run; it needs an owner decision on time, storage and the build path

Native IndexRead latency. The native Gate re-runs Current::check, with three TPM NV anchor reads, at least twice per boundary call; the measured queries make at least 95,000 to 342,000 such checks each. That cost is not measured here
A native-selected endpoint: no production code selects a generation, and the native Query arm refuses every query in a production build
The native Gate, Reader, prelude, grant validation, original read admission or the CLI; the observed path mirrors their shape only
The cost of the per-hit source/lifecycle proof reads, which the fixture's current_candidate does not perform
Cold-cache, concurrent, crash or power-loss latency
Per-match proof of total_matches; counts are bound to the exact current corpus root only
